Test_Cases.Feature: AHB interface to access its register space
Test_Cases.Test Description: Verifies the I2C register map by checking default values and then performing masked write-read verification across the defined register set. Any mismatch or access that violates declared read/write masks results in a failure.
Test_Cases.Remarks: Some registers are intentionally skipped for read or write based on the declared masks or skip flags. The soft reset helper is present in source but is not executed in this test flow.
Test Steps / Procedure: Test entry is invoked and begins with the default value verification sequence.

For each register index from 0 to the configured count minus one: obtain the target register from the register list. If the read mask for this index is zero, skip reading this register. Otherwise, read the register and compare the value against its expected default; record a default mismatch if the values differ.

Proceed to the masked write and read verification using a sequence of six test patterns. For each pattern, iterate the entire register list and write the current pattern to each register that is not flagged to skip and that is writable per the write mask.

After completing the writes for the current pattern, iterate the register list again. For each register that is not skipped and is both writable and readable per its masks, read the register and compute the expected value using the current pattern and masks; record a write-read mismatch if the read value differs from the computed expected value.
Upon completion of all patterns and checks, determine the final result: if any default mismatches or write-read mismatches were recorded, the test reports failure; otherwise, it reports success.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: During default checks, each readable register value must equal its documented default value.

During masked write-read checks, each readable and writable register must return the expected value derived from the current pattern and the defined read and write masks combined with the default value for masked-off bits.
Final outcome is a pass only when no default mismatches and no write-read mismatches are recorded.

Test_Cases.Test Description: Exercises a master-to-slave transfer between two controller instances configured for high-speed operation with DMA-based transmit and interrupt-driven flow control, followed by DMA-based reception and end-to-end data comparison.
Test_Cases.Remarks: System interface ports are configured as non-secure before enabling the transfer path. The test expects a transfer-complete interrupt and masks are configured to allow the event. DMA completion is polled until channels become idle.
Test Steps / Procedure: The test entry routine initializes state and configures system interface registers at offsets 0xA1700008 through 0xA1700054 to non-secure mode with the value 0x1.
Enable the interrupt lines in the interrupt controller and unmask the two controller interrupt sources in the system register block.
Clear pending interrupt status in both controller instances and set the FIFO flush for each one.
Program device control for both instances to enable operation; assign the slave address and the target address for the master.

Set the byte count to five on both instances and program the standard-mode low and high counts as well as the high-speed low and high counts; set the master code required for high-speed operation. Configure the interrupt mask to allow the transfer-complete event.
Set transmit and receive FIFO thresholds on both instances and enable DMA for the transmitting instance.
Prepare source data in memory starting at 0xA0243F00 by writing five ascending words.
Configure the DMA transmit channel to move five words from memory at 0xA0243F00 to the controller transmit data register space; enable the channel and wait until the channel becomes idle.
Start the transfer on the transmitting instance and repeatedly read the remaining byte count until it reaches zero, inserting short waits between reads.
Wait for the transfer-complete interrupt by polling a pending flag with short waits until it is deasserted by the interrupt handler.

Enable DMA reception on the receiving instance and configure the DMA receive channel to move five words from the controller receive data register space into memory starting at 0xA0243E00; enable the channel and wait until it becomes idle.
Read back the five sent words from 0xA0243F00 and the five received words from 0xA0243E00 and compare them one by one; record an error if any pair mismatches.
Wait briefly and then report the accumulated error count as the final result.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: A transfer-complete interrupt must be observed during the operation and, once serviced and cleared, subsequent reads of the interrupt status and the corresponding system interrupt status reflect no pending condition.
After both DMA operations complete, the five words written to the transmit memory buffer must exactly match the five words captured in the receive memory buffer.
The final result indicates success only if no data mismatches are detected and the interrupt condition is properly cleared.

Test_Cases.Test Description: Performs a master-to-slave transfer between two controller instances in standard mode using DMA to move data into and out of the controller FIFOs and an interrupt to signal completion, followed by memory-to-memory verification.
Test_Cases.Remarks: System interface ports are set to non-secure prior to enabling interrupts and transfers. A transfer-complete interrupt is required and must be acknowledged and cleared in both the controller and system registers. DMA completion is confirmed by polling the channel enable state.
Test Steps / Procedure: The test entry routine configures system interface registers at offsets 0xA1700008 through 0xA1700054 to non-secure mode by writing 0x1 to each.
Enable the relevant interrupt lines in the interrupt controller and unmask the two controller interrupts in the system register block.
Clear pending interrupt status in both controller instances and flush both FIFOs.
Program device control for both instances to enable operation; set the slave address and the master’s target address.
Program a five-byte transfer on both instances and set the standard-mode low and high counts. Configure the interrupt mask to allow the transfer-complete event.
Set transmit and receive FIFO thresholds on both instances and enable DMA for the transmitting instance.
Write five ascending words into memory starting at 0xA0243FC0 to seed the transmit path.
Configure the DMA transmit channel to fetch five words from 0xA0243FC0 and write them into the controller’s transmit data block; enable the channel and wait until it becomes idle.
Start the transfer on the transmitting instance and poll the current byte count until it reaches zero, inserting long waits between polls.
Set a flag to wait for the interrupt and poll until the interrupt handler clears it, inserting short waits.

Enable DMA on the receiving instance and configure a receive channel to transfer five words from the controller’s receive data block to memory at 0xA0243FE0; enable the channel and wait until it becomes idle.
Read back the five words from the transmit and receive memory buffers and compare each pair; accumulate an error on any mismatch.
Insert a brief wait and report the accumulated error count as the final result.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Transfer-complete interrupt must be detected; after clearing the controller’s interrupt and updating the system raw status, both the controller and system indicate no pending interrupt.
All five words written to the transmit buffer at 0xA0243FC0 must match the five words received at 0xA0243FE0.
The final outcome is a pass when no data mismatches are found and interrupt clearing is successful.
